layers.scope: Breakdown partitions full Markdown BPE tokens by the first byte's line: model_body is published unit explain, summary, extras and uncertainties; signature_location includes shared source-file reference definitions (including ones used by relations); heading_anchor, relations, footer, INDEX and node_text (including labels/whitespace) partition the rest. model_body/source and published_markdown/source use complete frozen files. semantic: all published Markdown (node pages + INDEX, including navigation, signatures and commands); deterministic: catalog.json as serialized, including preserved prose copies and edge references, excluding the graph field; frozen graph is excluded from token ratios (frozen_graph_tokens=0), reported separately as frozen_graph_bytes using UTF-8 JSON with ensure_ascii=False and compact separators; complete graph evidence is expanded only with query --edges; source: complete frozen files counted once; context source chunks, host prompts, raw answers and summary.json excluded; layers are storage measures, not disjoint content classes

issues: grp:format.h-countl-zero: says the fallback returns num_bits for zero input, but countl_zero_fallback(0) never terminates (n stays 0, the MSB test never succeeds), so there is no such return value.
grp:format.h-uint128: attributes the high-half overflow assert to operator+=(uint64_t), but that overload is noexcept and asserts nothing; the FMT_ASSERT(new_hi >= hi_) lives in operator+=(uint128).

grp:format-inl.h-rotr: says r==0 leaves the value unchanged and that a full-width shift is avoided, but the code computes n << 32 (or n << 64) when r==0, which is undefined behavior rather than a no-op.
grp:format-inl.h-error-reporting-helpers: says do_report_error writes the message plus a newline, but the newline is only written when fwrite returns >0; a failed write emits no newline.
grp:format-inl.h-system-error-reporting: says report_system_error prints to stderr with a newline, but do_report_error only writes the newline when fwrite returns >0.
grp:core.h-basic-specs-accessors: says each setter clears its field's bits before OR-ing, but set_upper, set_alt, and set_localized only OR the bit (and clear_alt clears it).
grp:core.h-check-for-duplicate: says names are pointer-equal, but the code compares named_args[i].name == arg_name, which converts the pointer to basic_string_view and compares contents.
grp:core.h-use-format-as-traits: says views are not auto-mapped for safety, but the trait only checks that the format_as result is arithmetic and does not exclude view types.
grp:core.h-fstring: says the const S& constructor performs the same view-lvalue static_assert as the array constructor, but it only runs the parse check and has no such static_assert.
grp:core.h-parse-format-specs: says only X/B set uppercase, but E/F/G/A also set uppercase before parsing the float presentation type.
include/fmt/core.h::function::detail.compare::14081: says it returns -1/0/1, but the memcmp path returns memcmp's unspecified negative/positive value.
grp:core.h-basic-string-view: says the template constructor accepts std-string-like types via data()/size(), but it also requires S::value_type to equal Char.
include/fmt/core.h::struct::FMT_END_EXPORT.type_mapper::38514: says long collapses to int or long long depending on sizeof, but long_short also requires FMT_BUILTIN_TYPES.
grp:core.h-parse-replacement-field: omits the failure when the format string ends immediately after '{', which calls on_error("invalid format string").
grp:core.h-compile-parse-context: says check_dynamic_spec reports when the referenced argument exists and is non-integral, but it also requires types_ to be non-null.

grp:chrono.h-to-nonnegative-int: says the integral overload rejects values ≥ upper, but the code rejects only values > upper (and the floating overload allows values below upper+1), so the stated [0, upper) contract is wrong.
grp:chrono.h-tm-field-accessors: says tm_hour12 maps h≥12 to h-12, but the code maps 12 to 12 (only 13–23 become 1–11).
grp:chrono.h-tm-writer-spec-handlers: says alternative-numeric paths delegate to format_localized, but on_utc_offset's alternative path calls format_utc_offset and hand-writes the colon instead.

include/fmt/chrono.h::class::detail.tm_writer::40480::s9: claims every on_* callback switches to locale_writer for non-classic/alternative numeric systems, but on_utc_offset, on_tz_name, on_iso_week_based_year, on_24_hour_time and on_iso_time do not follow that policy.

include/fmt/ostream.h::function::FMT_BEGIN_NAMESPACE.write_buffer::1467: says any ostream write failure propagates as an exception from os.write, but the code only calls os.write without setting an exception mask, so a failed write may only set stream state.

include/fmt/ostream.h::function::vprint::3627: says a recognized file buffer causes the stream to be flushed, but the code flushes only when _isatty(fd) is true; non-tty file buffers fall through without flushing.

grp:std.h-bit-reference-formatter: says detection requires convertible-to-bool, nothrow-assignable-from-bool, and flip(), but is_bit_reference_like has a libc++ specialization forcing true for std::__bit_const_reference<C>, so the formatter can be enabled without those conditions.

grp:std.h-variant-formatter: says the catch writes 'valueless by exception' instead, but the code discards the iterator returned by detail::write, so for non-appending output iterators the following ')' overwrites the first character.
grp:color.h-ansi-color-escape: says the emphasis constructor with no emphasis writes ESC '[' 'm', but the code overwrites the '[' with 'm' and produces ESC 'm'.

grp:args.h-dynamic-format-arg-store: says reference wrappers and non-string/cstring/custom types are stored by reference, but push_back(const T&) unwraps and passes them to emplace_arg, whose basic_format_arg stores built-in values by value; the named non-copy branch likewise stores built-in values by value.
include/fmt/fmt-c.h::module_region::FMT_MAKE_ARG::3119: says pointers map to fmt_from_ptr, but the _Generic cases only map void* and const void*; other pointer types fall to fmt_unsupported_type.

include/fmt/fmt-c.h::module_region::FMT_MAKE_ARG::3119: says unsupported arguments fail at link time, but fmt_unsupported_type is declared with no parameters and the macro calls it with (x), so the failure is a compile-time argument-count error.
grp:fmt-c.h-c-api-argument-types: calls the union anonymous, but the source union is the named member `value`, so members are accessed through `arg.value` rather than directly on fmt_arg.
grp:ranges.h-range-formatter: says a remaining ':' after the switch delegates to the underlying parser, but the 's' case returns immediately after consuming 's', so following specs are not parsed.
grp:printf.h-sprintf: says the char overload takes non-const argument references, but the source takes const T&.
grp:xchar.h-join-overloads: says every overload is enabled only when the deduced Char is not char, but the initializer_list overload has no such enable_if and is always available for wchar_t.

grp:printf.h-basic-printf-context and include/fmt/printf.h::function::FMT_BEGIN_EXPORT::392::s0: assert that arg() returns a disengaged/empty argument for an absent id, but the supplied source only delegates to args_.get and does not establish that fallback.
include/fmt/printf.h::function::detail.vprintf::13671: omits that a parsed argument index of 0 is rejected with "argument not found" before argument lookup.
grp:compile.h-runtime-named-field: says it writes each matching named argument, but the fold short-circuits after the first match, so later matching named arguments are not written.

include/fmt/compile.h::function::FMT_END_EXPORT.compile_format_string::12204: says specs after an unresolved name return unknown_format, but the static_assert requires dynamic names to be allowed first; otherwise compilation fails instead of returning unknown_format.
src/os.cc::function::file::9415: says _wsopen_s uses the default 0666 mode, but the source passes default_open_mode, which on Windows is _S_IREAD|_S_IWRITE (0600), not 0666.
src/os.cc::function::file::9415: says the helper is MSVC-Windows-only, but its source guard is _WIN32 && !__MINGW32__, so non-MinGW Windows toolchains also compile it.
